requirements.requirement: A local account named opsadmin exists on node1.
requirements.summary: opsadmin was absent initially, was created with the local useradd utility, and was directly observed before and after restart with UID/GID 1001, Bash as its shell, /home/opsadmin as its home, and a set password.

requirements.requirement: opsadmin has a private home directory.
requirements.summary: /home/opsadmin was directly observed before and after restart as owned by opsadmin:opsadmin with mode 0700. It was writable by opsadmin and unreadable by nobody.

opsadmin belongs to wheel, whose sudo policy permits all commands, and a validated root-owned sudoers entry was installed. Actual noninteractive sudo execution as opsadmin returned effective UID 0 both before and after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct pre- and post-restart observations. The provider-wide restart protocol for the sole managed node is complete and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities.
limitations: Native package-health collection timed out both before and after execution, so package consistency could not be independently compared (global:before_prepare:node1:package-health; global:after_executor:node1:package-health).

The exact dedicated sudoers rule text is masked in cmd-da08543ff4094b9b, but the visible wheel policy, wheel membership, successful syntax checks, and repeated effective-UID-0 executions provide strong direct evidence of full privileges.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Account creation, password assignment, home ownership/mode changes, and sudoers installation directly established the requested outcomes; the sudoers staging file was removed in the same command. The remaining mutation was the mandatory provider restart, scheduled through a transient unit. The restart protocol captured the completed-task baseline, acknowledgement and disruption, a changed boot ID, and recovered system, SSH, root filesystem, account, home, and sudo state. Fixed lifecycle boot identities corroborate the restart. No failed services, additional listening services, or abandoned task files were observed afterward.
